guideline: expert human annotators rate the system output on a Likert scale from Very Bad to Very Good for fluency (Is the output grammatically correct and sound like it was written by a native speaker?), adequacy (does the output preserve the meaning of the input?), and accuracy (did the model make the desired edits according to the given edit instructions?)
Annotators rate each output on fluency (grammaticality and naturalness), adequacy (meaning preservation), and accuracy (whether the desired edits were made).

each annotator is shown an instructional input and output from the model and asked to rate the quality of the output on three criteria: fluency (Is the output grammatically correct and sound like it was written by a native speaker of the language?), adequacy (does the output preserve the meaning of the input?), and accuracy (did the model make the desired edits according to the given edit instructions?)
